I'm happy to implement this in Chromium as an external contributor. Idk if that counts me as 1 implementor for the purposes of the WhatWG?

Once it's deemed this PR is wanted I'll happily go and file the necessary bugs and write any web platform tests needed.

s/showPicker() element/showPicker() method/

…in the first sentence of the issue description
In principle WebKit is supportive of this change, but we'd like some clarity on #9757.
@emilio do you or any other gecko folks have any thoughts on this?
At a glance it seems fine. CC @evilpie who implemented `showPicker()`. Can you file a mozilla standards position issue? That's the way of getting a more official position :)
Have made draft MDN PRs for this feature. All that's left is a resolution to https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/9757 for WebKit and I think this should be good to go?

Note that draft implementations do not suffice as implementer support; what you need is some commitment that the people in charge of approving shipping, are willing to do so. For Chromium that involves the Intent to Ship process; for Firefox that involves the Mozilla standards-positions repository, as has been requested already.
Okay I was planning on waiting till this PR was merged for filing the intent to ship but if its meant to be done before this gets merged that's fine. I'll get that filed tomorrow.
Seems as though mozillians and webkittens are supportive of this, based on the comments here and in the standards positions issues.
I've filled a chrome intent to ship as well https://groups.google.com/a/chromium.org/g/blink-dev/c/qew_ILTXWSY/m/AxHrcWzuAQAJ so I guess once that gets 3 LGTMs that's at least 1 solid interest

So I'm supportive of adding `showPicker` to `<select>` in principle. But I wanted to get one question answered: why didn't we include this with the original addition of `showPicker` for `<input>`? Was there a good reason? Or just because we were doing one thing at a time?

Assuming the answer to the above sounds reasonable, I'll take a look at the spec changes in this PR. But you can consider Chromium generally supportive.

https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/6909#issuecomment-959346224 suggests it was just deferred because input was more of a priority. The spec PR also mentions it as future work should it be asked for and https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/7957 effectively does that. I'm unable to find any concrete concerns with it that caused it to be deferred. But perhaps others have more context.

> [#6909 (comment)](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/6909#issuecomment-959346224) suggests it was just deferred because input was more of a priority. The spec PR also mentions it as future work should it be asked for and #7957 effectively does that. I'm unable to find any concrete concerns with it that caused it to be deferred. But perhaps others have more context.

Yep, thanks, that answers my question. Sounds like the only open question is https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/9757 then (also [raised by TAG](https://github.com/w3ctag/design-reviews/issues/900#issuecomment-1743258587)). Once that's resolved, this seems good to me. The spec text looks good also, no notes.

Regarding the focus question is that something that needs to block this or can it be a follow up PR? It applies to both inputs and select so it's tangential.

Also how best to get an answer to it? It sounds fine to optionally allow focus to me? Would Mozilla or Google be opposed to that?
I've added a sentence that hopefully addresses #9757 @annevk @zcorpan let me know if this is enough? (First time writing HTML spec sorry if it's not worded great)

I've added a line that says the picker user interface must be focused. Hopefully this addresses some of the accessibility concerns. As for whether the input/select itself can be focused (a requirement for iOS) I've left #9757 open to discuss that further.

Hopefully the PR should be ready to go now. I filed the participation request form idk if I need to do anything else to get that check to pass?
Also as an FYI I have the 3 LGTMs on the Chromium intent to ship conditioned on this being merged. So we have two implementers on board explicitly and none opposed.
Anything else I can do to nudge this across the finish line?

Hey @lukewarlow, I'm sorry, but I'm still a little stuck on https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/9757#issuecomment-1764335199. I realize this is not adding anything new compared to what's already out there, but it seems problematic to me that the existing API is so wildly different across implementations for the disconnected case (when the element is not in the document tree). And also, that for the disconnected case which is reportedly a key use case there's essentially no way to position the widget. That seems like a rather big design flaw to me with the original feature that needs addressing first.

I'm not actually convinced that (out of dom input) would be the majority use case? Given it basically doesn't work, and I can't think how it would without representing the pickers with pseudo elements that can take positioning data and using web tech (which wouldn't be desirable for WebKit I imagine?). That also would go counter to not wishing to expose whether a picker is implemented.

Not really sure what the next steps here are?

If authors want the pickers without the input UI that suggests to me that this is entirely the wrong path to go down and we really should be asking OpenUI to investigate exposing the pickers themselves as usable (stylable) elements?

Again not sure what WebKit would think of that as they are keen on native looking elements?

Have opened https://github.com/openui/open-ui/issues/922 to start this discussion to see if open ui are interested etc
https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/9912 - uses the algorithm defined in here so I've copied this change across removing the IDL additions. This will need rebasing if that gets merged first.
I think it makes sense to require that the `select` element be rendered for `showPicker()` to work. It can be extended later if we figure out how it should work in different browsers and devices.
@zcorpan do you envisage any wording changes to the spec?

In the `showPicker()` steps, just before calling "Show the picker, if applicable":

> If *this*  is a `select` element or an `input` element whose `type` attribute is not in the File Upload state, and *this* is not [being rendered](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/rendering.html#being-rendered), then throw a "NotSupportedError" DOMException.
Chromium currently supports showing picker for more than the file type (when not rendered). Should I just do the if this is select bit and ignore input entirely for now?

I've added that line but only with reference to select due to the comment above. @annevk would that be enough to alleviate concerns? If not is there anything else I can do to help move things forwards :)
That seems reasonable to me. @domenic thoughts?

OK. It seems the picker is rendered in the top-left corner for hidden non-file input types in chromium.

I suggested `NotSupportedError`, but maybe `NotAllowedError` is also appropriate.

> I suggested NotSupportedError, but maybe NotAllowedError is also appropriate.

Apologies I missed that. Will fix that now.

> @domenic thoughts?

I continue to think that a major use case for these will be showing the mobile full-screen pickers, which don't need a visible element to anchor to. I think that's how showPicker() is often used today on, e.g., date pickers.

However, I recognize that we haven't done good work on that front. We've made it too easy to create a good experience on mobile (e.g. a full-screen date picker) and a bad experience on desktop (e.g. no date picker in Firefox/Safari, or a date picker anchored to the top-left of the screen in Chrome).

So, taking a different route for select, where it just isn't possible to create a good experience on either mobile or desktop, seems like a reasonable first step. I hope we can do some work to allow all controls to work well on all platforms at some point though.

(Note that on iOS a select box dropdown is not fullscreen either. It used to be displayed in the keyboard area, but these days it is inline similar to desktop. So you would need some kind of coordinate system for some mobile platforms as well.)
